provenance.paper_title: Task-Driven Perception and Manipulation for Constrained Placement of Unknown Objects

latest_version.version_label: arXiv v1 / IEEE RA-L 2020 paper reviewed on 2026-08-31

representation_paths.memory_component: dynamic object-centric voxel representation with occupied and unseen sets

evidence.section: Full paper: Secs. III-IV Problem Setup and Proposed Pipeline
evidence.paraphrase: The robot maintains an object-frame voxel representation split into observed occupied surface voxels and still-unseen voxels. Conservative and optimistic object volumes derived from these sets are queried to plan safe grasps, sensing viewpoints, handoffs and constrained placements.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. IV Proposed Pipeline
evidence.paraphrase: After each new RGB-D viewpoint, transformed observations add previously unseen surface voxels to the occupied set and remove voxels shown to be empty. Grasps and placements are then recomputed over the updated object estimate under a fixed update rule.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. IV and online-adaptation description
evidence.paraphrase: Pose tracking corrects the object pose after stochastic in-hand motion, and the new registered depth observation revises occupied, unseen and empty-space assignments before the next manipulation plan is selected.

adjudication_notes: Included as an embodied-memory system because the persistent RGB-D-derived voxel state is operationally necessary for later sensing and manipulation actions, not merely an offline reconstruction artifact.

Strict-tier full-paper review: the object representation and pose are updated during task execution, while voxel-assignment, viewpoint-selection and replanning procedures remain fixed; therefore the highest tier is T2 and no T3 target is assigned.
